finding: §1 records that "spec-coverage is the only auditor id that changes routing" but no later section acts on it. spec-coverage is an ordinary corpus role (internal/engine/corpus/*/auditors/spec-coverage.json), so enabled: false applies to it, and routeChecklist gives it every spec-derived checklist item while all other auditors receive only file_check items (internal/cli/audit_roles.go:288, audit_routing_test.go:57-78). Deactivating spec-coverage alone therefore leaves the audit phase non-empty — §2.5 does not fire — while no auditor receives any spec-derived item, so an audit round can record all-PASS and drive convergence with the spec's own coverage never checked. Non-Goal 4 protects review's convergence machinery (regression) from exactly this failure mode; the audit-side equivalent is left unprotected, and CLAUDE.md's rule that implementation audit always runs to full convergence assumes it cannot be hollowed out.

suggestion: Decide explicitly for spec-coverage: either add it to Non-Goal 4's exemption (routing machinery, not a lens), or specify a dedicated refusal/warning in §2.5 for "the phase's spec-derived checklist has no recipient", and pin it with a test. Either way §1's routing sentence should point at the section that handles it instead of standing alone.

finding: Clause 1 enumerates the modes the refusal must NOT fire in (--record, --status, --merge, --resolve, --resolve-all, --verify, --report) and defines the refusal as firing in "prompt-emission mode", but it never mentions --perspective. As written the refusal fires on `tp review --perspective documentation` for a spec that deactivated every reviewer, killing a run that has nothing to do with the role panel — or, if the implementer decides otherwise, the exemption is invented behavior with no test (test 8 only enumerates clause 1).

finding: "Open" is defined for review as "a recorded finding surviving `reviewFindingResolvedAway`", but that predicate (internal/engine/reviewclean.go:32-43) excludes only resolutions with status wontfix or duplicate — a finding resolved **fixed** (the normal disposition, `tp review --resolve <file> <idx> fixed "evidence"`) still survives it. Under the stated definition, every deactivated role that ever authored a finding in any recorded round warns forever, even when all of its findings were fixed rounds ago and the phase has since converged. The audit half is scoped to the latest recorded round and therefore self-clears; the review half never does. An implementer cannot tell whether the intended set is "survives the round-cleanliness predicate" (as written) or "not yet dispositioned at all" (what the word "open" and the warning's purpose imply), and the two produce opposite output on every mature spec.

finding: Item 8 ('The same spec exits **0** under every other mode of each command, enumerated per §2.5 clause 1') is unwritable for several of the enumerated modes, because their exit code encodes state rather than the absence of the refusal. `tp review --status --check` exits 1 (`review_status.go`: `if check && (!converged || !allPass) { os.Exit(ExitValidation) }`) whenever the spec is unconverged — and the fixture for this test is a spec that has just been refused, i.e. with zero recorded rounds, so it is unconverged by construction and can never exit 0. `tp audit --status --check` has the same shape. `--merge`, `--resolve`, `--resolve-all`, `--verify` and `--report` additionally require inputs the item does not specify (an NDJSON file, a finding index and disposition, `--findings`), and exit non-zero when those are absent or when the merged set is empty. So the item, as pinned, asserts an outcome the tool does not produce.

resolved.evidence: §6 item 8 rewritten: each mode is asserted against its own contract (--record and --merge exit 0; --status --check exits 0 or 1 by convergence, never 2) and the assertion is the absence of the empty-phase error message rather than a non-2 code. suggestion: Either scope item 8 to the modes that legitimately return 0 on a bare spec and give each remaining mode its own expected code (e.g. `--status --check` → 1 for 'unconverged, not refused'), or replace the exit-code assertion with a refusal-specific observable: assert the refusal's message/hint literal from §2.5 is absent from stderr and no `.tp-review/<spec>/` write occurred, which distinguishes it from a malformed-argument exit 2 without depending on state-encoded codes.

finding: Test 8 requires the same spec to exit 0 "under every other mode of each command, enumerated per §2.5 clause 1". The other enumerated modes are not exit-0 either without extra operands — --merge needs input files, --resolve/--resolve-all need a findings file plus index and disposition, --verify needs --findings — each of which exits 2 or 3 on its own. Test 8's stated rationale (assert 0, not "not 2") therefore fails for reasons unrelated to the refusal leaking.
